## Root cause

`Interval.fromISO` (src/interval.js:134) called `DateTime.fromISO(s, opts)` / `DateTime.fromISO(e, opts)` directly and then tested `start.isValid` / `end.isValid`. When `Settings.throwOnInvalid === true`, `DateTime.fromISO` does **not** return an invalid DateTime — `DateTime.invalid()` throws `InvalidDateTimeError` (src/datetime.js:860-861). So:

1. A **valid** interval written in duration form (e.g. `"2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M"` or `"P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00"`) threw `InvalidDateTimeError`, because the duration half was first fed to `DateTime.fromISO` and that throw escaped `fromISO` before the `Duration.fromISO` fallback could run.
2. Invalid input (e.g. `"invalid"`, `"foo/bar"`, `null`) threw `InvalidDateTimeError` from the inner `DateTime.fromISO` instead of the appropriate `InvalidIntervalError` from the trailing `Interval.invalid("unparsable", ...)`.

The trailing `Interval.invalid(...)` call already had the correct `Settings.throwOnInvalid` → `InvalidIntervalError` logic (src/interval.js:66-78), it was just never reached. Additionally the explanation string was mangled: `can't be parsed asISO 8601` instead of `can't be parsed as ISO 8601` (compare src/duration.js:265, src/datetime.js:175).

## Fix (only file changed: /luxon/src/interval.js, lines 134-172)

Wrapped each `DateTime.fromISO` call in try/catch and captured validity in local booleans, so a throw from `DateTime.fromISO` (throwOnInvalid mode) is treated as "this half isn't a DateTime" and parsing falls through to the `Duration.fromISO` fallback and finally to `Interval.invalid(...)` (which throws `InvalidIntervalError` when `Settings.throwOnInvalid`, or returns an invalid Interval otherwise). Also corrected the message to `can't be parsed as ISO 8601`.
